status.en: 17 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 70% more than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Espriella and Catatumbo.
status.nb: 17 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 70 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Espriella og Catatumbo.

summary.en: ELN guerrillas deployed an armed drone to kill a soldier in Cauca while the Colombian Air Force bombed an ELN camp, killing at least three combatants. FARC dissidents executed three car bombs on the Panamerican Highway within seven days and a separate car bomb exploded outside a toll booth in Cauca, prompting a Colombian army airstrike that killed four suspected rebels, including a teenager. A Colombian peace tribunal charged former FARC members with anti-Indigenous crimes and war crimes against Indigenous groups. The United Kingdom pledged to continue championing the 2016 peace agreement at the UN Security Council. 225 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: ELN-guerrillaer satte i drift en bevæpnet drone for å drepe en soldat i Cauca, mens den colombianske luftforsvaret bombet en ELN-leir og drepte minst tre kampere. FARC-dissidenter utførte tre bilbomber på Panamerican-veien innen syv dager, og en separat bilbombe eksploderte utenfor en bomstasjon i Cauca, noe som førte til et luftangrep fra den colombianske hæren som drepte fire mistenkte opprørere, inkludert en tenåring. En colombiansk fredsdomstol anklaget tidligere FARC-medlemmer for anti-urfolk-forbrytelser og krigsforbrytelser mot urfolksgrupper. Storbritannia lovet å fortsette å forsvare 2016‑avtalen om fred i FNs sikkerhetsråd. 225 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
